job.style: a passage rich in numbers, dates or measurements

passage: Energy production methods vary significantly in their impact and operation. Solar photovoltaic panels convert sunlight directly into electricity using the photoelectric effect, which relies on light intensity rather than high ambient temperatures. In contrast, wind turbines function by capturing the kinetic energy of moving air to rotate blades, which then drive a generator to produce electricity. Hydroelectric power plants utilize the potential energy of water stored at a height in a reservoir; as water flows downward, it gains kinetic energy to spin turbines, demonstrating that energy is transformed rather than created from nothing. Furthermore, nuclear power plants generate electricity through controlled fission reactions in a reactor core, producing steam that turns turbines. The white plumes often seen rising from these plants are merely water vapor released from cooling towers, not radioactive gases. While some energy sources like solar and wind are renewable, they are not infinite; their long-term availability depends on sustainable management and infrastructure. Conversely, non-renewable sources like fossil fuels are finite because they take millions of years to form, meaning they cannot be replenished on a human timescale. Understanding these distinctions is vital for managing our global energy consumption, which currently exceeds 160,000 terawatt-hours annually, to ensure a stable future for the planet.

items.evidence: Solar photovoltaic panels convert sunlight directly into electricity using the photoelectric effect, which relies on light intensity rather than high ambient temperatures.
items.q: Two identical solar panels get equal sunlight. One is in a hot desert, one in a cool hill. What happens?
options: Both give about the same electricity
The hot desert panel gives much more
The cool hill panel gives much more
Neither works without extra heat from the sun
items.explain: Panels depend on light intensity, not on how hot the air is, so equal light gives similar output.

wrong.why: thinks solar panels work better in hot weather
thinks cold weather helps the panel more
thinks panels need heat, not light

items.evidence: In contrast, wind turbines function by capturing the kinetic energy of moving air to rotate blades, which then drive a generator to produce electricity.
items.q: A windmill's blades spin fast on a breezy day. What is the cause of the spinning?
options: Moving air pushes the blades round
The generator makes the air move
The blades first create the wind
Electricity inside turns the blades
items.explain: Moving air has kinetic energy that rotates the blades, which then drive the generator.

wrong.why: reverses cause and effect between generator and air
thinks spinning blades create the wind
reverses the order of electricity and rotation

items.evidence: Hydroelectric power plants utilize the potential energy of water stored at a height in a reservoir; as water flows downward, it gains kinetic energy to spin turbines, demonstrating that energy is transformed rather than created from nothing.
items.q: How does a dam's stored water end up spinning the turbines?
options: Its height energy changes into motion energy
It makes new energy from nothing at all
It is pumped upward to push the blades
Its heat energy turns into steam power
items.explain: Water stored high has potential energy, which turns into kinetic energy as it falls and spins turbines.

wrong.why: thinks dams create energy from nothing
reverses the direction the water flows
mixes up with nuclear plants that use steam

items.evidence: The white plumes often seen rising from these plants are merely water vapor released from cooling towers, not radioactive gases.
items.q: A child sees white clouds above a nuclear plant tower. What are they?
options: Water vapour from the cooling towers
Radioactive gas escaping from the reactor
Smoke from burning fossil fuels inside
Steam that has turned into poisonous dust
items.explain: The white plumes are only water vapour from cooling towers, not radioactive gases.

wrong.why: thinks all plants burn fuel and make smoke

items.evidence: While some energy sources like solar and wind are renewable, they are not infinite; their long-term availability depends on sustainable management and infrastructure.
items.q: Why can a renewable source still run short if people use it carelessly?
options: It is not infinite and needs good management
It can never run out whatever we do
It is finite because it takes millions of years
It is used up once, like fossil fuels
items.explain: Renewable sources are not infinite; lasting supply depends on sustainable management and infrastructure.

wrong.why: thinks renewable sources can never be exhausted
mixes up renewable with fossil fuel formation
thinks renewable sources are used up like non-renewable ones
